inputs.source: Support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors

instructions.note: The prompt directs reset and delivery based on the ticket opener, which implies the opener is authorized to receive the temporary pass.
The design relies on the prompt to require approval, rather than showing a separate enforced gate for all sensitive outcomes.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is enforced outside the model and shows the exact target account, requester, and full ticket text, but effectiveness degrades operationally at high request volume through approval fatigue.

controls.name: Bind temporary pass delivery to the account owner from the identity record
controls.decay_rationale: A destination confirmation bound to the system of record would prevent model- or requester-chosen recipients from receiving the temporary pass.

controls.name: Human approval gate on temporary pass delivery with recipient confirmation
controls.decay_rationale: The current gate covers the reset action but not the outbound delivery of the temporary pass. A separate delivery gate would add a review point for the actual recipient and payload.

findings.title: Confused deputy: untrusted ticket requester can obtain a temporary pass for the target account

attack_path.note: Contractors and vendors can submit ticket content and requester identity by email.
The agent looks up the target user profile and group memberships.
The agent can remove MFA methods and issue a temporary pass after analyst approval.
The temporary pass is sent to whoever opened the ticket rather than the account owner.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to resolve MFA problems by looking up the user, resetting MFA, and sending the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
The analyst sees the reset action, exact target account, requester, and full ticket body, but the shown approval is for idp.reset_mfa rather than for outbound delivery of the temporary pass.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, so the requester field is attacker-controllable untrusted input.
The temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner, creating a direct credential-delivery path from ticket requester to privileged account access.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, indicating high approval volume and approval fatigue risk.

recommendations.action: Bind temporary pass delivery to the account owner or a system-of-record recovery channel instead of the ticket opener.
Gate the actual temporary-pass send action with recipient confirmation, not only the MFA reset action.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or narrowed, approval volume remains high, or model/runtime changes increase unattended tasking while the send action still lacks a recipient-bound control.

findings.title: Human-agent trust exploitation: high-volume analyst approval gate on MFA reset is prone to consent fatigue

attack_path.note: Untrusted ticket text and requester identity drive approval requests.
Reset is blocked on analyst approval, but reviewers process a large routine queue.

evidence.observation: Every reset requires analyst approval before it runs.
The approval view exposes the raw action, exact target account, requester, and full ticket text.
Two analysts cover the queue and approve about 400 requests per shift; most are routine, which is high approval volume under the rubric.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, so the queue receives requests derived from untrusted sources.

recommendations.action: Reduce approval load with upstream identity verification and auto-reject rules for requester/account mismatches before analyst review.

forecast.watch_signal: Per-reviewer approvals stay high or rise, remembered approvals are introduced, or the approval gate is narrowed or removed.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe agent authentication surfaces or whether other systems can impersonate this agent.
No source or runtime configuration details say whether prompts or tool bindings are pinned against unauthorized change.
The design shows a short ticket-resolution workflow and no spend, loop, or recursive delegation capability in the provided artifacts.
This inbound flow can trigger individual reset requests, but the artifacts do not show queue exhaustion or resource-spend behavior as a design concern.
The outbound temp-pass message is a single delivery flow and the artifacts do not show volumetric or availability impacts on this edge.

rating.rationale: Manual validation only; scripts could not be run in this environment. The present design has a critical path from an untrusted ticket to restricted credential recovery: the requester can be an external email sender, the agent reads user data, resets MFA after a high-volume approval gate, and sends the temporary pass to the ticket opener rather than the account owner. The declared approval control lowers the reset-only finding by one tier because it is a raw-action gate with high volume, but it does not cover the send action and therefore does not reduce the end-to-end confused-deputy path. Forecast remains critical because any autonomy increase or gate removal defeats the only declared preventive control while the recipient-binding gap remains open.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, identity workflow specification, or enforcement configuration was provided, so control verification is limited to declared behavior and queue screenshots.
No logging, audit, or recipient-channel authentication artifacts were provided, so repudiation and delivery-channel assurances are only partially assessed.
